title: How to do deadlifts for SIZE
summary: NH argues bodybuilders need deadlifts: a natural hip hinge that gives a unique weighted stretch to the upper back and the biggest full-body stimulus, but not enough alone for full back development. He defends weighted stretch and partials for the traps, explains why deadlifts should be positive-only with no negative, and calls a neutral-back deadlift the safest compound lift, to be done at low frequency with straps.
claims: Saying deadlifts are unnatural is wrong; picking something up from the floor in a hip hinge is more natural than a horizontal press
Bodybuilders do what makes muscle grow, whether it is natural or functional or not
Conventional, sumo, trap bar and behind-the-back deadlifts differ in torso angle, knee flexion and hip flexion, so they are different movements
The deadlift works glutes, lower back, hamstrings, some quads, the entire upper back, forearms, arms, shoulders and neck: the most full-body compound
What the deadlift adds over other hip hinges is a weighted stretch for the upper back; good mornings don't stretch the upper back
Cutting all pulls from the floor out of a program hurts progress
Width comes from muscles like the outer lats and medial delts; thickness from muscles surrounded by other muscle like lower back, mid and lower traps
You don't have to do conventional deadlifts or mixed grip to prove manhood; some people aren't built for conventional
The more muscle a compound recruits, the more diffuse the stimulus, so some muscles you think you're hitting barely get worked
Powerlifting gave the deadlift a godlike status; no sport owns a movement
Deadlifts alone won't develop rear delts, lats and some traps; only deadlifting gives a 'surfboard back', thick with no width
He used to have a surfboard back from only deadlifting after falling for the deadlift meme
A few people with particular leverages grow lats from deadlifts thanks to the weighted stretch, but they are exceptions
Balance deadlifts with vertical and horizontal pulls for full back development
For size, torso angle in the deadlift dictates how much tension and stretch is applied across the body
Weighted stretch is not a meme; any negative is a weighted stretch
The upper back and traps grow from deadlifts without any elbow flexion or shrugging, so weighted stretch works
Starting the deadlift with shoulders over the bar and torso leaning in recruits a lot of mid and lower traps
Block or rack pulls below the knee allow more load and recruit more upper back, though not more posterior chain
Upper traps are mostly stimulated past the knee near lockout, so above-knee rack pulls are excellent for upper trap hypertrophy
Above-knee rack pulls are not a hip hinge anymore and carry over poorly to the deadlift
Farmer's walks and partial deadlifts both build the traps through isometric weighted stretch
Partials reduce lumbar involvement and save the lower back, but there is always a way to pull from below the knee with good technique
People call the deadlift's fatigue-to-stimulus ratio low because their poor form makes it fatiguing; a proper deadlift isn't very fatiguing
If you need lumbar flexion to get the bar up, you are deadlifting wrong
Do deadlifts positive-only: lift, put it down, reset; this lets you lift more weight
In hip hinges and squats the negative is never the limiting factor; you fail on the positive or the reversal
With help on the positive, you could probably do at least 40 extra negative reps of RDLs, because resisting gravity is much easier than fighting it
Positive-only deadlifts build strength in the positive, which carries over to other hip hinges done with negatives
Done properly, the deadlift is one of the safest lifts because there's no negative-to-positive reversal and you can just drop the bar
Deadlifts work well with low frequency, high intensity and moderate volume: every week or 10 days is enough
Hip hinges with a deadlift start, like RDLs, paused deadlifts and snatch grip deadlifts, all feed the deadlift
A heavy negative after a positive comes when you're already fatigued, which is a recipe for injury, unlike squat and bench where the negative comes first
Find a stance that allows a neutral back and leg drive: sumo, trap bar or blocks below the knee all work; behind-the-back is not recommended
Use straps; mixed grip makes no sense for bodybuilders
Lower back pain after deadlifts means you are not deadlifting properly
Deadlift only a few times a month and never every day or every two days; treat it as a very intense positive-only movement
He deadlifts every week and pulls from the floor all the time in his program
exercises: neutral back, push with legs, positive only, straps
